name: Do preventive maintenance on fleet equipment
summary: Planners watch engine and pump hours and raise a work order when a unit is due, then agree with operations when the unit can come off the fleet. Heavy-duty mechanics, fluid end and power end technicians and electrical technicians service the engine, transmission, pump and controls in a shop bay or on the pad between moves, test the unit and return it to the ready line. The work competes with keeping fleets working: pumps run 18 or more hours a day, parts were short in 2021-2022, and hour readings and checklists are re-keyed by hand, so services slip and defects found during service turn into repairs.

baseline.org_archetype: A Canadian pressure pumping company with six to eight crewed frac fleets, about 16 cementing units and six coiled tubing crews, maintained from district shops in Alberta and northeast BC.
baseline.notes: Common practice of large WCSB pressure pumpers in 2019-2022: an ERP plant maintenance module for work orders, hour readings from engine controllers and the data van, paper or tablet checklists, spreadsheets and phone calls between shops and field crews.

trigger: A unit reaches its service interval by engine or pump hours, or returns to the base between jobs, and the planner raises a PM work order.
end_state: The unit is serviced, tested and back on the ready line, and the work order is closed with hours and parts recorded; or the PM is closed and a repair work order is opened for a defect found.

volume.seasonality: Steady through the drilling season with work orders spread between pad moves; much higher in spring break-up (March to May) when parked equipment is brought in for overhaul, and lower in summer slowdowns or in 2020 when fleets were parked.

evidence.note: Organisation file volume, checked against fleet size: about 190 frac pumps at about 330 hours a month need an engine service roughly every 250 hours and a power end oil change about every 500 hours (src2 gives 500 hours as a typical oil interval), giving about 250-300 pump work orders, plus monthly or quarterly services on about 320 tractors, trailers, blenders, cementing and coiled tubing units.

surge.cause: Spring break-up: road bans park the fleet and equipment comes into the shops for overhaul

evidence.note: Spring break-up weight limits reduce oilfield activity (src1); spring thaw road bans start when thaw depth reaches 25 cm (src6). Duration and shop multiplier are tier C, matching the organisation file.

About 30-40 minutes of planner time per work order (due list, work order, release, review, status) across 900 work orders; the rest of the 8 planners' time goes to repairs, iron, inspections and parts.
Engine, transmission and chassis service, lockout, close-out on about 900 work orders a month; the rest of the 75 shop technicians' time goes to repairs, inspections and builds.

roles.title: Fluid end and power end technician

evidence.note: Power end and fluid end service on pump work orders.
Controls, sensors and wiring checks on each work order.
Approves out-of-scope repairs found during service and reviews the backlog.
Picks and issues PM kits. The organisation file does not list this role on the process; it is in the supply chain unit.
Moves units in and out of the shop bays. The organisation file does not list this role on the process.

systems.name: Maintenance work order and equipment history module
ERP (finance, procurement, inventory, plant maintenance, billing)
Vehicle telematics and electronic driver logs
Data van acquisition and treatment monitoring system
Dispatch and crew scheduling board (scheduling module, whiteboards, spreadsheets)
Email, Microsoft Teams and mobile phones

resources.name: Heavy equipment service bay (drive-through bay with overhead crane) in a district maintenance shop
Frac pump unit (2,500 to 3,000 HHP, trailer mounted)
Crew pickup trucks and light vehicles

steps.name: Pull hour readings and build the due list
steps.description: The maintenance planner exports engine and pump hour readings from the engine controllers, telematics and the data van job summaries, and enters any paper readings from the yard log into the work order module. A spreadsheet compares each unit's hours since last service with its intervals (engine service about every 250 hours, power end oil about every 500 hours) and flags units due within the next pad.

error.defect_description: A missed or stale hour reading leaves a unit off the due list or lists it too early.

evidence.note: Oil replacement interval of about 500 hours (src2) and a 500-hour pump service target matched to pad moves (src3). Engine interval and minutes are tier C.

steps.name: Raise the PM work order and reserve the kit
steps.description: The planner creates a preventive work order against the unit number in the ERP maintenance module, attaches the task list for the service level due and reserves the standard parts kit (filters, oils, packing, valve and seat sets). Hours and the last service date are copied from the spreadsheet.

error.defect_description: Wrong task list or kit for the unit's engine or pump model.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of heavy equipment maintenance in WCSB pressure pumping companies.

steps.name: Pick and stage the parts kit
steps.description: A warehouse attendant prints the reservation, picks the filters, oils and wear parts, issues them to the work order in the ERP and stages them on a cart at the bay. When the shelf count is wrong or a part is short, the attendant tells the planner.

error.defect_description: A part is issued to the wrong work order or not issued at all, so the work order cost is wrong.

next.condition: a part is short or the count is wrong

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of heavy equipment maintenance in WCSB pressure pumping companies.

steps.name: Requisition short parts
steps.description: The planner checks other bases' stock in the ERP, phones the nearest base to send the part on the next hot-shot, or raises a purchase requisition for the buyer marked with the unit's due date.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of heavy equipment maintenance in WCSB pressure pumping companies.

steps.name: Wait for the part to arrive
steps.description: The part comes from another base or from a supplier in Calgary, Edmonton or the United States. In 2021-2022 lead times on engine and pump parts stretched and some kits waited weeks; the unit keeps working past its interval or is parked.

evidence.note: Long lead times on key parts and record supply chain inflation in 2022 (src1). Wait durations are tier C.

steps.name: Agree a release window with operations
steps.description: The planner calls or emails the frac operations coordinator or district dispatcher to agree when the unit can come off the fleet, usually between pads or when a spare pump can take its place. If the unit is staying on a pad through a short move, they agree to service it on location instead.

next.condition: serviced on the pad between moves

evidence.note: Maintaining equipment between pad moves (src3). Split between shop and pad and waits are tier C.

steps.name: Bring the unit into a shop bay
steps.description: A yard operator moves the washed unit from the yard into a free service bay with a tractor or yard truck, chocks it and hands the keys and the work order to the technician. Units wait in the yard when every bay is taken by repairs.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of heavy equipment maintenance in WCSB pressure pumping companies.

steps.name: Drive the service truck to the pad
steps.description: Two heavy-duty technicians, one of them experienced on pumps, load the kit, oils and a parts washer into a service truck and drive to the pad, often two to four hours from the base on highway and lease roads. They check in with the frac field supervisor and wait for the pumps to be shut down at the end of the last stage.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of heavy equipment maintenance in WCSB pressure pumping companies.

steps.name: Lock out and isolate the unit
steps.description: The technician shuts down the engine, applies a personal lock and tag to the battery disconnect and the engine start, bleeds pressure from the fluid end and discharge line, and tries to start the engine to verify isolation. On a pad the frac crew's group lockout box is used.
inputs: unit in bay or on pad

control.basis: Alberta OHS Code Part 15, sections 212-214: isolate machinery and equipment, verify isolation and apply personal locks before maintenance

evidence.note: Isolation, verification and personal locks required by OHS Code Part 15 (src5). Minutes tier C.

steps.name: Service the engine, transmission and chassis
steps.description: The heavy-duty technician drains and replaces engine and transmission oil, changes fuel, oil and air filters, takes an oil sample for the lab, checks belts, hoses, coolant, radiators and the trailer brakes, lights and tires against the checklist.

error.defect_description: A filter or drain plug is left loose or the wrong oil grade is used.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of heavy equipment maintenance in WCSB pressure pumping companies.

steps.name: Service the power end and fluid end
steps.description: On pump units the fluid end and power end technician changes the power end oil and filters, inspects plungers, packing, valves and seats, replaces worn consumables, checks crosshead clearances and torques the fluid end bolts. On other unit types the step is a short check of pumps and hydraulics.

error.defect_description: Packing or a valve seat is not seated, giving a leak on the first pump run.

evidence.note: 500-hour oil and pump service intervals (src2, src3). Minutes and mix of unit types tier C.

steps.name: Check controls, sensors and wiring
steps.description: The electrical and instrumentation technician checks the engine and pump controller, pressure transducers, the remote control cable and lighting, reads stored fault codes with a laptop and replaces damaged connectors.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of heavy equipment maintenance in WCSB pressure pumping companies.

steps.name: Record findings and decide on defects
steps.description: The heavy-duty technician writes findings on the checklist and decides whether any defect found (a cracked bracket, a leaking cooler, a worn crosshead) is outside the PM scope. Small fixes are done now; larger ones need the shop manager.

error.defect_description: A developing defect is not written up and fails later in the field.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of heavy equipment maintenance in WCSB pressure pumping companies.

steps.name: Approve extra work or open a repair
steps.description: The shop manager looks at the defect, the parts needed and when operations needs the unit back, and either approves fixing it under the PM work order or opens a separate repair work order and releases the unit's PM as complete with a deferred defect.

control.basis: Company maintenance policy: work outside the PM task list needs shop manager approval and a separate repair order above a cost limit

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of heavy equipment maintenance in WCSB pressure pumping companies.

steps.name: Make the minor repair
steps.description: The technician replaces the cracked bracket, hose or cooler line using shop stock and adds the parts and hours to the work order.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of heavy equipment maintenance in WCSB pressure pumping companies.

steps.name: Run and test the unit
steps.description: The heavy-duty technician removes the locks after checking that all tools and people are clear, starts the engine, runs it to temperature and, on pumps, pumps water against a test choke at low pressure to look for leaks, knocks and abnormal temperatures.

control.basis: Alberta OHS Code Part 15, section 215.3: returning equipment to operation after locks are removed

next.condition: leak or fault found, back to service

evidence.note: Returning equipment to operation after lockout (src5). Test content and failure share tier C.

steps.name: Return the unit to the ready line
steps.description: A yard operator moves the unit out of the bay to the ready line, or on a pad the technicians hand it back to the frac field supervisor, who adds it to the pump line-up for the next pad.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of heavy equipment maintenance in WCSB pressure pumping companies.

steps.name: Close out the work order
steps.description: The technician types the labour hours, hour meter reading, parts used and findings from the paper checklist into the work order, attaches the oil sample label number and sets the status to technically complete.

error.defect_description: Hours, parts or the hour reading are missing or typed wrongly, so the next due date is wrong.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of heavy equipment maintenance in WCSB pressure pumping companies.

steps.name: Review and close the work order
steps.description: The planner checks the completed work order against the task list and parts issued, corrects the next due hours, raises iron certification or commercial vehicle inspection work orders when the unit's iron or annual inspection is due, and closes the order.

control.basis: Maintenance records kept per unit for warranty, insurer and customer audits of equipment maintenance programs

next.condition: sent back to the technician to correct

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of heavy equipment maintenance in WCSB pressure pumping companies.

steps.name: Update fleet availability
steps.description: The planner marks the unit available on the dispatch board and in the weekly fleet status spreadsheet, and emails district operations and the frac operations coordinators when a unit they were waiting for is ready.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of heavy equipment maintenance in WCSB pressure pumping companies.

exceptions.name: Short or missing part
exceptions.description: The kit is short because the shelf count was wrong or the part is on back order; the planner sources it from another base or a supplier and the unit runs past its interval or waits.

exceptions.name: Service on the pad
exceptions.description: The unit cannot come off the fleet, so two technicians drive to the pad and service it during the move between wells or pads.

exceptions.name: Defect found during service
exceptions.description: The technician finds a defect beyond the PM task list; half are fixed under the PM, the other half become repair work orders.

exceptions.name: Failed run test
exceptions.description: A leak or fault on the run test sends the unit back for rework.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from work order raised to closed in the maintenance module
benchmarks.population: Preventive work orders on frac, cementing and coiled tubing units and their tractors at a WCSB pressure pumper, 2019-2022

evidence.note: Author's estimate: release windows follow pad moves every few days to two weeks; the unit is usually back in service in one to three days and paperwork closes within a week. No published figure found.

benchmarks.population: Frac pump power ends (example interval in trade press)

evidence.note: Example of extending oil replacement intervals from 500 to 700 hours.

benchmarks.population: Frac pumps on continuous pad operations

evidence.note: Pumps clocking 18-22 hours a day; Canadian fleets in 2019-2022 ran fewer hours on average.
Ideal interval stated by an equipment supplier.

pain_points.description: Units that are making money on a pad are hard to release, so services slip past their interval and failures move into the field.

evidence.note: Maintenance timed to pad moves (src3); slippage is tier C.

pain_points.description: Parts shortages and wrong shelf counts hold up kits, worst in 2021-2022 when lead times stretched.

evidence.note: Long lead times on key parts (src1).

pain_points.description: Hour readings and paper checklists are re-keyed into the work order module days later, so due dates drift and work order costs are incomplete.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of common practice before connected telematics were fully linked to maintenance systems.

pain_points.description: In spring break-up every parked unit comes in at once and the shops run extended hours while bays are full.

evidence.note: Break-up activity drop (src1) and road bans (src6); shop congestion tier C.

sources.title: Trican Well Service Ltd. Management's Discussion and Analysis for the year ended December 31, 2022
sources.supports: Stainless steel fluid end costs of $7.5 million in 2022 and $8.0 million in 2021 ($1.2 million in Q4 2022) as the item that drives variability in repair and maintenance expense; higher active equipment raised repair and maintenance costs; personnel costs include operational support personnel such as mechanics; long lead times on key parts and record inflation in 2022; maintenance capital $29.96 million in 2022 and $23.5 million in 2021; fluid ends pump abrasive slurry at up to 15,000 psi and are modular units replaced independently of the power end; spring break-up road weight limits reduce oilfield activity; seven active and five parked frac crews in 2022.

sources.title: New Engines, Pumps Aid Frac Fleets (Frac Facts, August 2021)
sources.supports: Frac pumps clock 18 to 22 hours a day; example of extending oil replacement intervals from 500 to 700 hours; a condition-based service model raised average fluid end life by 400 hours.

sources.title: Extending Service Life Of Equipment Components Key To Improving Frac Efficiency (Frac Facts, January 2024)
sources.supports: An ideal pump and check valve repair interval is 500 hours, matching a four-well pad so equipment can be maintained between pad moves; a conventional spread uses 20 or more pumps including backups; in-place field maintenance is usually less cost-effective than it appears and maintenance is safer and faster with equipment shut down and lifting equipment available.

sources.title: Occupational Health and Safety Code, Part 15: Managing the Control of Hazardous Energy
sources.supports: Part 15 sections 212 (isolation of machinery, equipment or powered mobile equipment), 213 (verifying isolation), 214 (assigning personal locks), 215 (group control procedures), 215.3 (returning to operation) and 215.4 (isolation of piping). Current page; Part 15 was in force in an earlier edition in 2019-2022.

sources.title: Road bans
sources.supports: Road bans reduce maximum weights on roads during weak or thawing conditions; spring heavy haul weights start when thaw depth reaches 25 cm; provincial highway and municipal bans; exemptions by permit from the Central Permit Office.

assumptions: One work order covers one unit's scheduled service; pump units, tractors, trailers, blenders, cementing and coiled tubing units are mixed, and the touch ranges cover the mix (a tractor service takes one to two hours, a pump service four to eight).

The work order is raised by the planner when the yard logs a returned unit or when hour readings show a service due, so the trigger is the yard and base operations process as in the organisation file.

The organisation file lists the resource maintenance-shop with 5 items at about 500 hours a month (2,500 bay hours). Preventive and corrective work orders need roughly 6,000 to 12,000 bay hours a month, so this file models a service bay resource (about 40 bays across 5 shops) instead.
The frac-pump resource is held for the engine service step as a stand-in for the unit being out of service; for non-pump units the hours apply to the unit being serviced.

Staffing: about 41 FTE of shop technicians (heavy-duty, pump and E&I) plus planners, yard and warehouse staff, about 48 FTE in all, close to the hands-on time times 900 work orders a month at 130 productive hours per FTE. Shop technicians work extended hours, which explains why waits are short once a unit is in a bay.
Loaded costs are the organisation file's (wage x 1.35).
Simulated cycle time includes the paperwork tail (close-out and planner review); the unit is usually back on the ready line two to three days before the work order closes.
